newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits narrowly mixed ahead of CPI.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits narrowly mixed ahead of CPI.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were narrowly mixed in dull trade on Tuesday with most traders sidelined ahead of the release of the U.S. December consumer price index (CPI) and retail sales index data later in the day, dealers said.

The market is also waiting for more clues to market direction from U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's discussion on central banking and global finance at a seminar sponsored by Leuven Kul University in Belgium, at around 0930 GMT today, they said.

"Rates were a little bit mixed in the morning on some position adjustments. Everyone is waiting for tonight's CPI and retail sales figures, but I don't think there will be much impact unless the numbers are way off market expectations," a local dealer said.
"Some people are also waiting for the outcome of Alan Greespan's speech in Belgium today for fresh clues to market direction," he said.
In day-to-day rates, Tuesday/Wednesday eased 1/16 percentage point to 5-5/16 5-3/16 percent.
But Wednesday/Thursday and week-fixed rose 1/16 point each to a common 5-7/16 5-5/16 percent.

Among longer dates, two-months was unchanged from Monday's 5-1/2 5-3/8 percent, four-months unchanged at 5-9/16 5-7/16, six-months rose 1/16 point to 5-11/16 5-9/16 and twelve-months rose 1/16 point to 5-15/15 5-13/16 percent.
